questions.question: Q: List the stages of the Statistical Enquiry Cycle in order.

points.text: Plan, Collect, Process, Present, Interpret, Evaluate.

questions.question: Q: At which stage would you calculate the mean and range of a data set?
Q: At which stage would you draw a scatter graph to show the relationship between two variables?
Q: Why is the Evaluate stage important?

points.text: It allows you to assess the reliability and validity of your conclusions and to suggest improvements for future investigations.

questions.question: Q: How might the Evaluate stage lead back to the Plan stage?

points.text: If evaluation reveals flaws in the method or sampling, you may need to plan a revised investigation to obtain more reliable results.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response A student investigates whether taller people have larger shoe sizes. They collect heights and shoe sizes from 30 classmates, calculate the mean for each group, draw a scatter graph and conclude the hypothesis is supported. Identify the stage for each action. <div class="

points.text: 1. 'They collect heights and shoe sizes from 30 classmates' — Collect stage: gathering raw data. 2. 'Calculate the mean for each group' — Process stage: summarising the data using a statistic. 3. 'Draw a scatter graph' — Present stage: displaying the data visually. 4. 'Conclude the hypothesis is supported' — Interpret stage: drawing a conclusion and relating it to the hypothesis. The student should also carry out the Evaluate stage, assessing whether 30 classmates is a representative sample, whether there may be bias (e.g. all same age), and whether the method could be improved.
